question: 1. Display all unique department numbers from both EMP and DEPT tables.
2. Display all department numbers from EMP and DEPT including duplicates.
3. Display department numbers that are present in both EMP and DEPT.
4. Display department numbers that are present in EMP but not in DEPT.
5. Display department numbers that are present in DEPT but not assigned to any employee.
6. Display employee names and department names in a single column using UNION.
7. Display all employee names and department names, including duplicates.
8. Display jobs that exist in EMP table and also exist as department names.
9. Display employee names that are not department names.
10. Display department locations that are not used by any employee.
11. Display employee names from department 10 and department 20 using UNION.
12. Display employee names from department 10 and 20 including duplicates.
13. Employees who work in departments that exist in DEPT master table.
query:
SELECT ENAME FROM EMP 
WHERE DEPTNO IN (SELECT DEPTNO FROM EMP INTERSECT SELECT DEPTNO FROM DEPT);

question: 14. Employees whose department does not exist in DEPT table.
query:
SELECT ENAME FROM EMP 
WHERE DEPTNO IN (SELECT DEPTNO FROM EMP MINUS SELECT DEPTNO FROM DEPT);

question: 15. Dept numbers that have employees and also exist in master table.
16. Display all unique roles and department names in one result.
17. Display common values between employee job and department location.
18. Display employee names who are not assigned to any valid department.
19. Combine employees earning more than 2000 and employees from department 10.
20. Display employees who work in department 10 but NOT in department 20.
21. Dept numbers in both tables, but exclude department 10.
22. All employee names and department names sorted alphabetically.
query:
SELECT ENAME AS Name FROM EMP 
UNION 
SELECT DNAME FROM DEPT 
ORDER BY 1;

question: 23. Display department numbers that appear in EMP more than once.
24. Employees from departments in NEW YORK and DALLAS using UNION.
25. Combine Salary > 3000 and Job = 'MANAGER' results (No duplicates).
